title: Resolve tenant-claim reconciliation causing RBAC drift and KMS unwrap race in Private clusters
creator: Riley Chen
description:
Summary: A customer escalated an incident on 2026-03-09 where users on a Private deployment intermittently lost RBAC bindings after SSO logins; audit events for those denial episodes were not present and SSO assertion decoding intermittently failed with KMS unwrap errors. Impact affects a single large customer in eu-west-1 running Private (control plane managed, customer-managed KMS).

Scope & impact: Affects tenant-scoped RBAC evaluation in Private control plane across multiple clusters for that customer (estimated 20% of logins in a 12-hour window). Customer reported immediate production impact — several users unable to access internal features — and requested an urgent patch. Customer impact: high.

Reproduction steps observed in-house:
1) Configure a Private cluster with SAML IdP that emits a tenant claim (tenant_id) and a group list.
2) Rapid key rotation on customer KMS (rotated by external policy) while the control plane is processing concurrent assertions.
3) Identity service decodes SAML assertion -> normalizes NameID/tenant claim -> writes ephemeral mapping to tenancy table -> triggers RBAC evaluation.
4) Under race, KMS unwrap returns transient 'key not found' or 'wrong envelope' causing assertion decode to fail; decode path retries but uses cached (stale) tenant mapping for later requests.
5) Result: RBAC evaluator sees stale tenant mapping (old tenant namespace) for a subset of sessions, causing access denials; audit-logger batches drop the failed decode events because error metadata incorrectly classified as non-audit and was dropped by the background emitter.

Root cause hypothesis (confirmed by logs and debug traces):
- Two related issues combined to produce the outage: (A) race between KMS unwrap and assertion processing when KMS rotates: the unwrap path returned a transient unwrap error which we handled poorly (no robust retry with key ID lookup), and (B) tenant claim normalization path writes to an eventually-consistent tenant-mapping cache with a short TTL but no strong ordering; when unwrap recovers, subsequent requests could be evaluated against the stale mapping snapshot.
- Audit emitter had an edge-case where decode failures flagged as 'non-user-facing' were collapsed in the emitter's dedupe window; the emitter uses a background queue with a 60s dedupe that dropped certain transient decode failures.

Immediate mitigations applied (customer-facing and internal):
- 2026-03-10 06:00 UTC: Enabled control-plane shim that forces synchronous tenant-claim canonicalization before RBAC evaluation for the affected customer (applied as a targeted feature flag). This prevented new sessions from being evaluated against stale mappings.
- 2026-03-10 09:20 UTC: Increased KMS unwrap retry policy and added explicit key-id lookup fallback so unwrap errors are retried with authoritative key id resolution. Deployed to private-staging and then to the customer's control plane.
- 2026-03-11 02:00 UTC: Adjusted audit-emitter to treat assertion-decode failures as high-fidelity events (no dedupe) for 24h to capture the remaining events for the post-incident audit.
- Customer communication: Support PM notified customer (ticket #SUP-9871) with mitigations and next steps; customer accepted temporary mitigations and requested a durable fix.

Planned permanent fix (work in this ticket):
1) Identity service change: make tenant-claim write idempotent and strongly ordered per assertion using a lightweight per-tenant sequence number to avoid race windows; implement a two-phase write that is write-compatible with existing reads to avoid downtime.
2) KMS client: implement unwrap-with-keyid-first and aggressive retry with exponential backoff and jitter for transient wrap-key errors; add metrics and saturating circuit breaker to avoid flood when KMS is unavailable.
3) Audit pipeline: change classification so assertion-decode failures are always recorded (never silently dropped) and add a 'diagnostic' field to the audit events to capture KMS unwrap error codes.
4) Add an end-to-end integration test that simulates KMS rotation and asserts no RBAC drift and that audit events are emitted.

Rollback and rollout plan:
- Deploy fix to private-staging (canary environment) and run automated soak with a KMS rotation script for 24 hours.
- Canary rollout to 5% of production Private clusters (region-limited) with feature-flag gating and health checks (failed login rate, audit emission rate, unwrap error rate).
- Full rollout after 48h healthy canary. Rollback will be done by reverting the feature flag and re-applying the temporary shim.

Testing & QA:
- Unit tests for unwrap/backoff logic and tenant-sequence enforcement.
- Integration test harness that runs against a simulated KMS and SAML IdP to reproduce the race.
- Manual acceptance: run the customer's exact SAML metadata and rotation schedule in a mirrored staging customer instance.

Observability & metrics to monitor during rollout:
- unwrap_error_rate (by key-id), unwrap_retry_success_rate, unresolved_assertion_rate, login_denial_rate_by_tenant, audit_event_emission_rate, emitter_dedupe_drop_count.

Postmortem actions (deferred tasks):
- Patch docs: add troubleshooting steps for customers running external KMS and IdP rotation schedules.
- Create runbook for on-call: immediate steps when unwrap error spikes appear.
- Long-term: evaluate migrating audit buffer to write-through durable queue (Kafka) to avoid background-collapsing edge cases.

Notes: This ticket coordinates with security and platform teams because KMS policy touches customer-managed keys and audit retention changes may affect compliance. Security review required before wide rollout.
